Historical Evidence

These charts summarize the current Madison Metro Transit event export. Each row is a stop-level observation where two adjacent buses on the same route and direction were predicted to arrive closer together than the scheduled-headway threshold.

The current file covers 2026-09-09 to 2026-10-29 and contains 51,123 stop-level observations across 25 routes and 928 stops.

Counts are stop-level observations. A close bus pair can be counted at multiple downstream stops if it remains bunched along the route.

Daily observations

Shows how observations vary by service date in the current export. Spikes are useful review dates, not proof of a one-time external cause. Wednesday, Sep. 2 was the first day of UW-Madison classes; use that date as a before-and-after marker for campus travel patterns. The current event export starts after Sep. 2.

Shared Terms

Bus bunching

Two buses on the same route and direction arrive too close together.

Stop-level observation

A detected bunching case at one stop and snapshot. One close bus pair may produce multiple stop-level observations as it travels along the route.

Bunching severity

How close the buses were compared with the bunching threshold. Higher severity means the buses were closer together.

Recurring bunching

Repeat patterns by route, stop, day, or hour.

Non-recurring bunching

Spikes linked to incidents, detours, or other unusual operating conditions.
